Amputee Xolani Luvuno

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
From heroin-addicted street beggar to Comrades Marathon runner & iron-man competitor, this is the inspirational story of amputee athlete Xolani Luvano

Unique Selling Point:
Xolani Luvano has a truly inspirational story. He's an amputee who spent 10 years homeless and addicted to heroin. 3 years ago he was rescued from life on the streets by good samaritan Hein Venter. Since his rehabilitation, he's got a full-time job and gone onto run the Comrades Marathon and is training to compete in the grueling Iron Man on 7 April in Port Elizabeth.

Summary:
We tell the amazing story of Xolani Luvano. Hailing from the Eastern Cape, he spent his youth as a common criminal, stealing on the streets of Port Elizabeth. Then he discovered that he had bone cancer which resulted in his right leg having to be amputated. He ended up begging, spending the next 10 years homeless in PE, Durban and finally Centurion. Life on the streets is hard. He's had to beg and prostitute himself to feed his habit.

3 Years ago he was rescued by good samaritan Hein Venter who gave him shelter and a job at his perfume factory in Midrand. As part of his rehabilitation, Xolani began running with his work colleagues. This hobby fired Xolani's passion. Last year he took part and completed the Comrades Marathon, "running" the 98km race on crutches and one leg.

Now he's turned attention to the gruelling Iron Man and is training to take part in the race on 7 April.

We tell Xolani's inspirational story

Press Release:


Xolani Luvuno
Xolani Luvuno is an amputee who spent 10 years homeless and addicted to heroin. Three years ago he was rescued from life on the streets and replaced drug addiction with a passion for endurance sports, completing the Comrades Marathon on crutches last year. Last Sunday Luvuno faced his biggest challenge to date: The daunting Iron man triathlon. Carte Blanche meets the inspiring athlete.
Producer: Julian Sun
Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


INTRO VOICE OVER:

To be an endurance athlete takes more than mere desire

It requires the mental fortitude necessary to overcome pain

The discipline to endure hours of training

A lack of fear when it comes to failure

And to be in peak physical condition.


V/O: The Iron Man Triathlon is widely regarded as one of the most physically demanding single-day sporting events in the world.

It comprises a 3,8km ocean swim, a 180km bike ride and a 42km marathon.

For many it will be the hardest things they’ll ever do.

But the challenges of Iron Man are nothing compared to what Xolani Luvuno has had to overcome in his life.

V/O: Xolani Luvuno was born in the Eastern Cape. He was kicked out of home at just 16 because of drugs. Living on the streets of PE, he was arrested for house robbery and sentenced to 5 years in jail. Worse was to follow. Soon after his release, he noticed a pain in his right leg.

Xolani on discovering he had bone cancer and having to have his leg amputated.

Claire: Without a leg, his downward spiral continued. He turned to Nyaope for escape and spent the next 10 years begging on the streets.

But hope can come from the most unlikeliest of places and it was on this street corner here in Centurion that Xolani met local businessman Hein Venter.
Hein on meeting Xolani

V/O: Hein could not find a rehab willing to take him in so Xolani made the brave decision to quit drugs cold turkey.

Xolani on going cold turkey



V/O: The relief of weaning himself from drugs was matched by the joy of getting fitted with the prosthetic leg. For the first time in 7 years, Xolani would walk

Hein’s emotions about getting him a leg.


V/O: Xolani’s recovery has not been without its challenges. He may have quit drugs but the demon of alcohol soon reared its head.

Hein & Xolani tell the story of tough love
V/O: Xolani threw himself into his new passion: 5km became 10km, half marathon became a full marathon, and incredibly, just 2 years after he started running, Xolani completed his first Comrades on crutches in July 2018

Xolani & Hein on competing in X’s first Comrades.

Claire: Fresh from completing his very first Comrades Marathon, Xolani looked for his next challenge.

But what could be harder than running an ultra-marathon? How about the grueling iron man triathlon.

V/O: Andrew Brummer is a swim coach who has worked with many triathletes. Inspired by Xolani’s incredible story, he took it upon himself to become his swimming coach

Andrew Brummer on teaching Xolani how to swim

V/O: swimming is just one aspect of the Iron Man. Hein & Xolani would also have to prepare for a 180km cycle and a 42k marathon.

On taking part in Iron Man and training for it.
V/O: After months of hard work and training, Xolani & Hein took their place on the starting line in Nelson Mandela Bay this past Sunday.

The Iron Man’s fearsome reputation was proved, when sadly two other competitors lost their lives trying to finish the 1,6km ocean swim.

Unaware, Xolani & Hein completed their swim in 75minutes. Cheered on by the crowd they entered the transition area to prepare for the bike ride when Xolani tripped and fell, injuring his wrist in the process

It cost them precious time but eventually they made it onto the bike.

As the day progressed, a fierce headwind hampered their progress and when they eventually crossed the finish line at around 6pm, they discovered that they’d missed the cut-off by just 5 minutes.

Their race was run.

Xolani’s swollen wrist was examined at the medical tent.

Amazingly it was discovered by the medics that Xolani had ridden 180km with 2 broken bones in his hand.

Though he might not have completed the race, his determination to soldier on in spite of the pain, encapsulates the remarkable story of Xolani Luvuno.

In the face of adversity, he’s found a way to overcome the most overwhelming odds and never give up…the very definition of an Iron Man
